comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 History EER and student curriculum describe the 180 EC full-time Dutch-taught BA. The History track and Foundations of Europe are selected by official order. The major includes 60 EC of foundational courses, a 30 EC depth package, 15 EC of track-specific writing and historical foundations, and a 15 EC thesis. The four package courses and the writing and historical foundations courses require 45 EC at introductory level. Thesis entry requires 30 EC at advanced level and a qualifying Seminar A. The 60 EC profiling space includes a 30 EC coherent package and 30 EC of free electives. At least 15 EC of the profiling space must be at level 2 or 3.

Research Seminar B: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21015)
Historical Writing (GE2V17001)
components.note: The writing course and Foundations of History also require 45 EC at introductory level.

components.name: Bachelor’s Thesis in History (GE3V23001)
components.note: Students must earn at least 30 EC at advanced level and complete a qualifying Research Seminar A before starting the 15 EC thesis.

components.name: Coherent elective package
components.note: Choose a minor or approved study abroad. Across the full 60 EC of electives, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Options include individual courses, a second minor or an internship of up to 15 EC.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized Geschiedenis target does not select between the two formal tracks or among their seven depth packages. The adopted 2026-2027 OER lists Track Geschiedenis before Internationale betrekkingen in historisch perspectief and lists De fundamenten van Europa first within Track Geschiedenis. That package is therefore selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic historical identity, research methods and present-day relevance and responds most directly to the selected Foundations of Europe package through history, archaeology, art, religion, identity and material culture. Two further official, evidence-backed and feasible directions remain: International Relations in Historical Perspective, focused on world order, conflict and security; and Societal Challenges, focused on inequality, capitalism and prosperity. History education is assessed but rejected because UCR does not provide the sequenced pedagogy, school placement or teaching qualification implied by that later outcome. The three included curricula share the complete six-course UCR History sequence but diverge substantially in their adjacent disciplinary courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: UCR Modern History covers modernity, imperialism, war and decolonisation. Utrecht provides a dedicated contemporary history survey.
UCR History of Empires studies power, legitimacy and identity across empires. Utrecht concentrates on the foundations of Europe and the role of religion.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Research Seminar B: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21015).
UCR World Archaeology uses material sources to interpret ancient societies across regions. Utrecht approaches the ancient world through historical study.
UCR studies Renaissance Italy and Mediterranean exchange through art and material culture. Utrecht surveys a broader span of early modern and modern history.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Cities and Citizens (GE3V20011).
Both develop research questions, evaluate historical sources and write an argument. UCR’s course studies the American Century, while Utrecht’s seminar is part of the Foundations of Europe package.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Utrecht's compulsory course.
UCR introduces statistical analysis and research design. Utrecht applies data to historical questions.
Both develop systematic inquiry and source interpretation. UCR studies qualitative social research, while Utrecht teaches historical research.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Historical Writing (GE2V17001).
UCR examines how scholars interpret and write the history of art. Utrecht introduces history as a wider discipline.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Bachelor’s Thesis in History (GE3V23001).
No second scheduled UCR course reproduces Utrecht's full compulsory historical-research-laboratory sequence.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Utrecht's specified scope.
Utrecht's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.

Utrecht's remaining 30 EC is genuine free space, potentially including an internship; UCR choice is distributed across the liberal-arts curriculum and no one scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.
